Superconductivity

QTrans estimates the superconducting transition temperature using a simplified Allen-Dynes formula. The spectral definitions below use the isotropic, nonmagnetic, spin-degenerate case as the reference convention.

Eliashberg Spectral Function

Let \(N_F=N(\varepsilon_F)\) denote the electronic density of states per unit cell, per unit energy, and per spin at the Fermi energy \(\varepsilon_F\). The band sums below include one copy of each spin-degenerate band, and Brillouin-zone integrals are normalized by the Brillouin-zone volume \(\Omega_{\mathrm{BZ}}\). The variable \(\omega\) denotes angular frequency, and the electron-phonon coupling matrix element \(g_{\mu\nu b}(\mathbf{k},\mathbf{q})\) has units of energy.

In this convention, define the phonon linewidth parameter in angular-frequency units as

\[\gamma_{\mathbf{q}b} = 2\pi\omega_{\mathbf{q}b}\sum_{\mu\nu} \int_{\mathrm{BZ}}\frac{d^3k}{\Omega_{\mathrm{BZ}}} |g_{\mu\nu b}(\mathbf{k},\mathbf{q})|^2 \delta(\varepsilon_{\nu\mathbf{k}}-\varepsilon_F) \delta(\varepsilon_{\mu\mathbf{k+q}}-\varepsilon_F).\]

The corresponding energy linewidth parameter is \(\hbar\gamma_{\mathbf{q}b}\). The Eliashberg spectral function is

\[\alpha^2F(\omega) = \frac{1}{2\pi\hbar N_F}\sum_b \int_{\mathrm{BZ}}\frac{d^3q}{\Omega_{\mathrm{BZ}}} \frac{\gamma_{\mathbf{q}b}}{\omega_{\mathbf{q}b}} \delta(\omega-\omega_{\mathbf{q}b}).\]

This normalization agrees with the ordinary Eliashberg spectral function in Resistivity. The dimensionless electron–phonon coupling constant is

\[\lambda=2\int_0^\infty\frac{d\omega}{\omega}\alpha^2F(\omega).\]

The factor of 2 in this frequency integral is part of the definition of \(\lambda\); it is not an additional spin degeneracy factor. Spin counting must instead be consistent between the electronic band sums and \(N_F\).

For \(\lambda>0\), the logarithmic average phonon frequency is

\[\omega_{\mathrm{log}} = \exp\left[ \frac{2}{\lambda}\int_0^\infty\frac{d\omega}{\omega} \alpha^2F(\omega)\log\left(\omega\right) \right].\]

These integrals assume a dynamically stable phonon spectrum with positive frequencies; imaginary modes require a separate assessment of structural stability.

Allen-Dynes Critical Temperature

The simplified Allen-Dynes expression implemented in QTrans is

\[T_{\mathrm{c}} = \frac{\hbar\omega_{\mathrm{log}}}{1.2k_{\mathrm{B}}} \exp\left[-\frac{1.04(1+\lambda)} {\lambda-\mu^*(1+0.62\lambda)}\right],\]

where \(\mu^*\) is the dimensionless effective Coulomb pseudopotential. This semi-empirical estimate describes isotropic, phonon-mediated pairing. The full Allen-Dynes formula contains additional strong-coupling and spectral-shape correction factors \(f_1f_2\); these factors are set to unity in the current implementation. The simplified estimate should therefore be used with care for strongly coupled or strongly anisotropic systems.

QTrans returns \(T_{\mathrm{c}}=0\) when \(\lambda-\mu^*(1+0.62\lambda)\leq0\). This is an implementation convention outside the attractive regime of the estimate, rather than a general criterion for the absence of superconductivity. The exponential is evaluated only when the denominator is positive.

Note

Internally, QTrans uses phonon energies in Hartree. The logarithmic average returned by the code is therefore the energy \(E_{\mathrm{log}}=\hbar\omega_{\mathrm{log}}\). The code evaluates \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T_{\mathrm{c}}\) in Hartree and converts the result to kelvin for output. The spectral coordinate in a2f.dat is an energy in meV, despite being labeled omega.
